categories.name: Realtors specialising in lots, acreage & teardowns
categories.opportunity: Buyers of lots and teardown properties need to know what they can build and for how much before they firm up. Agents who can bring a builder for a quick feasibility check close more land deals.
categories.rationale: A builder who helps a land buyer decide becomes the obvious choice to build, months before the project is tendered.

triggers.event: A buyer makes a conditional offer on a lot or teardown
triggers.whyNeed: They need a budget and feasibility assessment

categories.mutualValue: Agents close land sales; you meet clients at the start of their project.
categories.approach: Offer agents a 48-hour feasibility and budget-range review for their land buyers.
categories.decisionMaker: Agent who lists or sells land and teardown properties
categories.regulatoryNote: Real estate registrants' referral-fee rules generally prohibit paying non-registrants.

categories.name: Construction-mortgage lenders & brokers
categories.opportunity: Construction mortgages advance in draws against completed stages, so lenders vet the builder, the budget, and the schedule. Brokers are asked which builders produce cost breakdowns lenders accept.
categories.rationale: Financing is a gate every custom build passes through, and builders who make draws smooth become the broker's default recommendation.

triggers.event: A client applies for a construction mortgage
triggers.whyNeed: The lender requires a builder's contract, budget, and draw schedule

categories.mutualValue: Brokers close construction files; you get financed clients. You can refer clients needing financing back.
categories.approach: Prepare a lender-ready budget and draw-schedule template, and meet brokers who handle construction financing.

categories.name: Land-use planners & surveyors
categories.opportunity: Owners pursuing severances, minor variances, or rezoning to create a buildable lot work with planners and surveyors long before choosing a builder.
categories.rationale: These professionals see future building projects at the approval stage.

triggers.event: A severance or variance is approved

categories.mutualValue: Planners gain a builder who can advise clients on buildability; you get early access to projects.
categories.approach: Offer planners a builder's perspective on constructability and cost during approvals.
categories.decisionMaker: Land-use planner or Ontario Land Surveyor

assumptions: Custom builds start long before construction: with a land purchase, a severance, financing, or a design. Builders who are present at those decisions win projects without competing on price alone.
No typical project value was provided, so commercial-value ratings are relative to the industry, not your own pricing.

guardrails.title: Partnerships are not paid-referral arrangements
guardrails.body: This analysis recommends building relationships based on mutual value. It does not assume that referral fees, commissions, exclusivity, or endorsements are permitted in your industry. Check professional, regulatory, and contractual rules before compensating anyone for referrals.

guardrails.title: Outreach in Canada: CASL applies
guardrails.body: Commercial electronic messages generally need express or implied consent, sender identification, and a working unsubscribe mechanism. Implied consent can exist when a business email address is conspicuously published, the message relates to the recipient's role, and they have not said they don't want such messages. Keep records of how consent was obtained. Personal information you collect is also subject to privacy law (e.g. PIPEDA).

guardrails.title: No automated outreach
guardrails.body: This tool does not contact anyone on your behalf. Every introduction should be personal, relevant to the recipient, and easy to decline.
